newsitem.title: HONG KONG: "Censorship" row, HK council blocks handover rally.
newsitem.headline: "Censorship" row, HK council blocks handover rally.

text.p: A Hong Kong local authority came under attack for "censorship" on Tuesday when it blocked a bid by democracy activists to organise a rally on July 1 when the territory reverts to China.

The Urban Council voted down a second request by the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of the Patriotic Democratic Movement in China to stage a public meeting in Victoria Park, named after Britain's 19th century empress.

"You can imagine that's a purely, you know, a kind of political censorship, (to) try to block the Alliance to use Victoria Park (for) a rally," said Fred Li, a Democratic Party councillor and legislator.
Alliance chairman Szeto Wah had filed the second request in a week to use the park for the rally.
The alliance was spawned by the 1989 student-led pro-democracy protests in Beijing, which ended in a bloody military crackdown with a heavy toll of life.

China brands the organisation subversive, and has launched moves to crimp protest rights and other civil liberties after Britain returns Hong Kong to China in two weeks time, ending 156 years of colonial rule.

The grouping, Hong Kong's main mass movement campaigning for greater democracy in China and Hong Kong, planned the protest march to test Beijing's pledge that Hong Kong's way of life and free expression will survive the change of flag.
Szeto said the group would now look elsewhere.

City-centre Victoria Park is the traditional venue of an annual candlelit vigil in remembrance of the June 4, 1989, Tiananmen Square crackdown. About 55,000 people attended the Hong Kong vigil this year.
